transcript.text: Samsung microwave runs, light on, plate turns, fan going, but the food comes out stone cold. Watched a YouTube video on testing the magnetron - I've got the cover screws out already, what should I check first?

I can't guide any testing or work inside a microwave — the high-voltage capacitor can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged, so the casing should only be opened by a qualified engineer. Please do not touch the internal components or test the magnetron yourself; microwaves contain high-voltage capacitors that can hold a lethal charge even when unplugged. The most common reasons for this are either the appliance being set to a low power level (like Defrost) or a fault in the heating circuit. To help narrow this down, were you using a standard 'Full Power' or 'Auto Cook' setting, or was it on Defrost/Low Power/Grill?
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
It wasn't on defrost, I tried full power and other levels and it's the same on all. A cup of water for a minute stays cold. The hum is also quieter than it used to be.

As mentioned previously, the high-voltage capacitor inside a microwave can hold a lethal charge even when unplugged, making this work strictly for qualified engineers. The quieter hum suggests the magnetron is likely failing to oscillate properly, which suggests a fault in the high-voltage heating circuit (such as the magnetron itself, the HV diode, or the transformer). Please stop using the appliance and contact a professional repair service or the manufacturer for a safe diagnosis and fix.
